utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth. The interpreters, are you there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to the Prosecution, the Defence, Mr. Krstic, the court reporters, the legal assistants. We are still in the same composition, and we are here to continue the hearing of the Krstic case. According to what I see in front of me, it is Mr. McCloskey. Yes, will you please tell us what we're going to do today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have a witness that will be testifying, a woman. We're going back to Potocari briefly and she will be testifying in open session. Her name is Hava Hajdarevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I was waiting for the interpretation. Mr. Usher, can you have the witness brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: She has her earphones on under her scarf, so you may want to make sure they work and all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for coming here to the Tribunal. Before testifying, you are going to read the solemn declaration, which the usher will give you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, for the moment you will be answering questions which the Prosecutor, Mr. McCloskey, who is standing to your right, is going to put to you. Mr. McCloskey, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, can you tell us your name, and spell your last name, please.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: My surname is Hajdarevic; my name, Hava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you spell your surname?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: H-a-j-d-a-r-e-v-i-c.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The first letter is "H". I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old are you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you Muslim by faith?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are you from?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: From Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend most of your life in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you living there on July 11th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in Srebrenica were you living?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I was living at the exit from the town, towards Potocari, towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were you living with then?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I had two sons, a daughter-in-law, and a two-and-a-half-year-old granddaughter. Then my mother came to stay. My brothers and sisters-in-law, they were living with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your husband at the time?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: My husband was captured, and in 1994 he was exchanged and then he was in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he wasn't in Srebrenica in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't in Srebrenica, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on July 11th that caused you to make a decision?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I had to leave the house because the Serb army entered the town from up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did the presence of the Serb army make you have to leave?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Because they would have killed me, I wouldn't exist now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you decide to go, and who went with you?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I decided to go to UNPROFOR to seek their protection, and from there to go to Tuzla, and my whole family went with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was in your family that went with you to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: With me were a daughter-in-law and a sister-in-law, my brother's two children, my granddaughter, and my mother. And the other sister-in-law and brother were living in town and they also went to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were your two sons adult age at that time?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: They were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: They went through the woods. We parted there, with my brothers and sons, and we went to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have three brothers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I now have one and two of them are gone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you haven't seen two of your brothers and your two sons since they left to go through the woods; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: That is right. I never saw them again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you went to UNPROFOR, was that in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you stay when you got to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: It was the afternoon, on the 11th. We wanted to go to UNPROFOR. The UNPROFOR wouldn't let us go any further, there was a ribbon across the road, so we stayed behind where the hangars are and the Zinc Factory and the garages. And we asked to be put up somewhere, and I spent the night next to the zinc plant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next day, did Serb soldiers arrive some day to Potocari, the next day, on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time did you first notice Serb soldiers arriving?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember exactly now. I think it was about noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about what you saw?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I saw some of them coming from the woods, towards Pecista. They were coming downhill; they were burning things and shooting. And another group were coming from Bratunac, together with Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell what things were burning?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Mostly the old houses and haystacks, so as to intimidate us. And we were watching all that because there was a hillside and we were down in the valley and we could see what was happening on the slopes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see General Mladic arrive?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I did. I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see happen after he arrived?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: UNPROFOR had those ribbons across the road, and he came up there and they probably didn't let him enter. So he returned towards Bratunac, from where his group was coming, and then he joined the group and they walked in among the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: What happened? I went back to my mother and daughter-in-law and sister-in-law. The children started crying. There was panic. We were, indeed, afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything else that day?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I saw -- this was later, I had spent the night by the zinc plant. Then I took my family and we entered the factory to spend the night inside. Since the soldiers started walking around among the people, then they started taking out our young men and taking them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were these soldiers dressed like?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: They were dressed in military camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. How do I know? They had black gloves with their fingers showing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They weren't Dutch soldiers.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No, not then, no. The first night we were safe. The Dutch soldiers were protecting us. We were okay that first night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the night of the 11th that you were safe; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the soldiers started taking men away, what did you do with your family?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: When I saw four soldiers bringing ten young men and taking them away, then I became scared and I realised what would happen. And then I took my family and we went along the road and spent the night inside an old bus, to be as close as possible to UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any Serbs that you were able to recognise from before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I only saw my neighbour, Slavoljub. Towards nightfall, he was going towards the garages. He had a black uniform on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his last name?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Grujicic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how old was he?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Slavoljub, he's an older man. Maybe 60 or something. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did he have any sons that you knew from before the war?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: He had five sons. We were all living in one neighbourhood. We were friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you name some of the sons of Slavoljub?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: One was Cvijetin, Dzole, Mile, Vitomir, and the youngest one I can't remember. He was the youngest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Slavoljub, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't really see what he had on him. I hid from him so he wouldn't see me, because they did approach us and ask us about our men. They would ask the women about the men and he would have recognised me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see the group that Slavoljub was with, the group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were five or six of them all in black clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before you hid from them, could you see what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About what time was this that you saw these soldiers in black including Slavoljub Grujicic?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: It was at nightfall, it was already dark. He was moving in the direction of the garages down there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about where did you see him, about where was he when you saw him in relation to the various factories and the main road?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: There's a small bridge and there used to be a kind of reception hut there and then you go towards the garages, and that is where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was he near the -- near the various factories around the base?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: He was below the road, the other side of the road below the factories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you spend the night that night?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I spent the night there, close to this bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in around or in one of the old derelict buses that was in and around the bus factory?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: It was a bus. There was a path leading to the garages. The buses of Strela Company used to be parked there. And then to the left, there was an old bus. And there was an outpatient's clinic at Potocari and next to it was this old bus and we spent the night next to this bus. I think there are pictures of those buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe what you heard or saw that night, this would be the night of the 12th?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I heard the worst. I heard people screaming, crying and Ohran was calling out the name of his cousin, "Ahmed, have they killed you, have they slaughtered you?" They were wailing. It was a terrible night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there screams going on throughout most of the night?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything that was happening around you that night?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: That is all I heard. And then you could see the people sleeping on the ground next to the garages and then UNPROFOR, it looked like UNPROFOR walking amongst those people. What they were doing, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next morning, what did you do the next morning with your family on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: The next morning, I got up. I told my family to hurry up and go towards the personnel carrier. And I saw this Ohran who had been calling his sisters on the previous night, his head was all covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Then we went as quickly as we could towards the buses where they were parked. They all were from Serbia, 7th of July, Raketa, Vagevo; these are the names of the bus companies. They had taken away our men. We got on to a bus; I think it belonged to the 7th of July Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you got on the bus, did you see a Dutch soldier on top of a vehicle at some point?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: This was when the Serb soldiers entered. This might have been towards darkfall when you are going towards Srebrenica. There was a vehicle, an UNPROFOR vehicle, and on it there was a soldier lying on his back. Why and how, I don't know. It was so hot, why would he have been lying like that if he hadn't been captured or something?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually see him tied down or did you just see him lying on this vehicle in this heat?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I just saw him lying on his back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he might have just been lying in the sun for all you know?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't imagine why a person would lie in the hot sun like that.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: That's what I think too. Why would he be lying like that facing the sun in that heat?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you got on the bus, where did you go and your family?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: We went towards Kladanj. We passed through Bratunac. We passed by Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything on the way towards Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: On a meadow, I saw our men, four rows of them. I don't know how many. I saw a man dressed in a white coat, and he was doing something to a man's head right next to the road. And the others were watching, those four rows of men. And then we went along the road and we came across our men with their hands like this [indicates], and soldiers pushing them along, that's what we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicated that her hands were on the top of her head, she saw her soldiers with their hands on top of their heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what villages you were near when you saw these men in the meadow, and then later on you saw men with their hands on their head?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: This was Sandici, Kravica, as far as Kasaba, that is the route we took; Sandici, Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back just briefly to when you saw Slavoljub. In one of your old statements, it also says that you saw his son, Cvijetin. Did you actually see his son Cvijetin?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: One of my neighbours, they were all there, but I left early in the morning, about 9.00. And all the others were there, Grujicics and Stevos, and they were all there. And a neighbour of mine asked him to save him but he left and he didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you see Cvijetin or did one of your neighbours tell you that she had seen him?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: She told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you actually see Slavoljub or did someone tell you that he was there?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I saw him towards nightfall on the Wednesday, on that Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you eventually let off the bus near Tisca where you had to walk a distance to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we got off there. We had two kilometres to cover to reach our territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you make that or did you eventually meet up with your husband?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: When I reached Tuzla, my husband had already left for Germany a month or two before that, I think, in January or February.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you have since been able to be reunited with your husband; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I was reunited when he came two months later to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to ask you this question, but I think the Court and, perhaps, the world would like to know. How is it living without your two sons and without your three brothers in the wake of the tragedy of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: How? You have children of your own. Only I know how I feel. I had two sons, now I don't have any, and I lost my brothers too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Hajdarevic, please have some rest. Take your time. If you need a break, we'll have a break. We understand how painful this must be for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you too, Your Honour. We could perhaps have a little break if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. So for the purpose of organising our work, Mr. Petrusic or Mr. Visnjic, how long do you think that the cross-examination will take?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not more than five minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then, we will still have a 15-minute break. I hope that you will be able to get some rest so that you can come back and continue with your testimony. A 15-minute break. --- Break taken at 10.08 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Hajdarevic, are you feeling any better now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm fine now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now you're going to answer questions that will be put to you by Mr. Visnjic, who is representing General Krstic in this case. Mr. Visnjic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Visnjic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Hajdarevic.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajdarevic, I should like to ask you a question regarding your neighbour Slavoljub Grujicic, the one you recognised in Potocari. Could you tell us whether you had had any argument with him before the war? Did you have any problems with him?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were in good relations before the war.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mrs. Hajdarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Visnjic. Any additional questions for the witness, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mrs. Hajdarevic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'm sorry to bring these memories back to you. You have lost two sons, you have lost three brothers. Did you get any information after they went away what happened to them or where they were?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: I learned about my sons, that they had reached Baljkovica, the crossing point, and that's all I know about them. As regards my brother, he was in Potocari and he was left there. My cousins, my relatives, they were among those who went to the woods, and I haven't heard of them ever since.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: "Ever since" means since July 1995?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Do you know many people in your family, in your acquaintance, who also passed through the same sad experiences, where their sons and brothers disappeared and they have no news?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. There are so many such cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The cases of people returning, were there cases of sons and brothers coming back?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that happened as well. Azim Begic, he had six sons, and all of them managed to cross over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were they in the woods?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Did they tell you what happened?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they told us various stories. There were lots of stories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. You mentioned that the UNPROFOR was walking among you with the Serbs, if I remember, and you were hearing screams at the same time. What were the UNPROFOR soldiers doing exactly?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: No, they were not UNPROFOR soldiers, they were Serb soldiers. They had taken their clothes and put them on. They were not members of UNPROFOR. UNPROFOR soldiers wouldn't do anything to us. They would have helped us, like they did on the first night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mean they were dressed as UNPROFOR, they had the UNPROFOR dress?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because they had captured both UNPROFOR members and us, and they did as they pleased with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'll ask you again about Azim's sons; he had six sons. The six sons came out of the woods, were able to come back?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, all of them, they reached Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: They said that many other people were able to get away from the woods, or were they exceptional?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, they know how it was. People kept coming out for months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Riad. Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I have no questions except to thank you for sharing your sad memories with us. I hope they will do the search for truth well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Hajdarevic, I have only one question to ask of you. I should like to know something about the soldiers who arrived on the 12th of July. You are not sure that they were Serbs; you just know that they were not Dutch. So my question is the following: Did you hear them speak?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was near them. They were taking away our young men, they were taking them to the Zinc Factory. Our mothers were crying, pulling them by their sleeves, telling them to let their sons go. Four of them were taken away, and then another ten, they were taken in the direction of Budak. But they were speaking our language; they were our people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're saying that they were speaking your language.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: In the army? No. No. They were all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So those soldiers were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you heard them speak, what were they saying?

utterances.speaker: HAVA HAJDAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were addressing the mothers who were there. They would, for example, tell her that they would only take her son for questioning and then that they would let him go. That's what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mrs. Hajdarevic, for coming here to the Tribunal. I should like to thank you once again, as my colleagues have done, for sharing with us your suffering. I hope that you will always be able to find reason to live, meaning in life, at least to tell us about the terrible things that have happened. Is there anything else that you should like to say, something you haven't had the opportunity to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should just like to ask one question of these gentlemen from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mrs. Hajdarevic, you cannot speak directly to these gentlemen, but perhaps you could ask a general question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The gentleman from Belgrade, does he have children?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I suppose he does.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then how could they have come here to defend a man like Krstic? This is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I hope that the world will be able to answer a question like this, and I hope that this will be an example of how people should be treated. Thank you very much once again, Mrs. Hajdarevic. I should like the usher to accompany Mrs. Hajdarevic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Before I turn the podium over to Mr. Harmon, who has the next witness, I just wanted you to know that in the future we will be providing evidence on the identities and the units of some of these people that these witnesses have identified. For example, Slavoljub Grujicic was a member of the Bratunac Brigade of the Drina Corps at the time, and you will see those records and witnesses will explain those records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I give the floor to Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours; good morning to my colleagues for the Defence. Our next witness will be a young man named Enver Husic, and he's going to testify without protection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall wait for him then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. You are going to read the solemn declaration that the usher will give you, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Are you comfortable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for coming. For the moment you will be answering questions put to you by Mr. Harmon, who is standing to your right. Mr. Harmon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Harmon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Husic.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to you relax. I'm going to ask you a number of questions about your experiences. Get comfortable. First of all, can you spell your last name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: My name is H-u-s-i-c, and my first name is E-n-v-e-r.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old are you, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I am 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the fall of the enclave in 1995, were you living in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom were you living?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I was living with my mother and father, two brothers and a sister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the time of the fall of the enclave, was your father in active duty in the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he registered as a soldier or did he actually go to the front line?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: He was just registered as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had two brothers. One brother was named Ramiz; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was Ramiz at the time of the fall of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Nineteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old were you at the time of the fall of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Seventeen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had one other brother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I understand it, your other brother passed away before the fall of the enclave; am I right on that?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when the enclave was attacked by the Bosnian Serb army, where did your mother and your sister go?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: They went to a place called Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you, Ramiz, your brother, and your father go?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: We went to a place called Kazani where there were many other people and we headed through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 7A placed on the ELMO. I'm going to show you a map and I'm going to ask you to identify certain places on Prosecutor's Exhibit 7A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the map, can you tell the Judges why was it that you and your father and your brother went through the woods?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: We went because the Serbs were shelling, shooting and we feared we would share the fate of many other people who had, during the war, been killed and slaughtered. And we went to the woods hoping we could reach free territory from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you take a look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 7A which is on the ELMO. Could you point to some of the locations in your journey where you went through the woods and before you actually surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could show the witness the map and then place it back on the ELMO; he's going to need to see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a look at that for just a second, Mr. Husic, and then we'll put it back on the ELMO and then I'd like you to indicate with the pointer your direction of flight.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you just place that back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the pointer, Mr. Husic, could you point for the Judges' benefit the direction of your flight from the time you left Kazani to the point of your surrender, and please point to the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: We passed through a place called Susnjari, Buljim, Kamenica, and then Sandici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I notice two of the maps -- two of the -- three of the areas are indicated on the map, Buljim is not indicated on the map. Could you point to the area of Buljim on this map since you mentioned it in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is the location [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating the circle in the middle, indicating there's a town in there called Bare, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how many people were gathered --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm finished with the exhibit, Mr. Usher, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you estimate how many people were gathered at Kazani before people left the enclave and went in the direction of Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact number, but there were a lot of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there women amongst the people gathered at Kazani?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were. I saw about ten women there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there children?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you describe the manner in which you left the enclave?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: First, we went along a wider road, a group of people. There were a lot of people. It wasn't a proper column across the fields to Buljim. We didn't go along roads, but across the fields a lot of the time. But from a distance, it looked like a column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell the Judges approximately your position in the column; were you in the front of the column, in the middle of the column, in the rear of the column?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: We were in the rear, not quite at the very end, but in the last half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date when you left the enclave?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was the 11th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, accompanying you in the column, were there men with rifles?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your part of the column, approximately how many men had rifles?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I could see about 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the purpose of the men with the rifles in your part of the column?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Their purpose was to protect the rear part of the column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, briefly, could you tell the Judges what happened once you left Srebrenica and before you surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: We reached Buljim from Kazani, that is Srebrenica. I fell asleep from fatigue. I woke up in the morning, it had dawned, and my father and brother were not there. They had left before me. So there were only a few people left in Buljim, and I was among them. There were about 50 armed Muslims there, soldiers, and I went down hill from Buljim towards Kamenica. The column was two by two. We went down hill, I saw four dead men. Then we went on. The path was marked with pieces of papers, because they told us that it was mined so we couldn't move away from those markings. The Serbs were shooting. I think they used mortars and infantry weapons and rifle grenades. A lot of people lost their lives there. Then, however, I found my father who was hit by an explosion of a rifle grenade. He wasn't feeling well. He wasn't really hit, but it was the detonation that had affected him. Then we went on, a place called Strane, the shooting stopped, we couldn't hear anything. We just heard the Serbs calling out to one another. At the same time, we suddenly heard something that sounded like the wind blowing and suddenly, the fire came from all sides. My father got up. I helped him go down towards a stream. I saw people falling. A lot of people were hit. And we managed to pull out somehow. We went along the stream and uphill. There weren't many people who had pulled out. We could hear screams and moans and shooting. And my father and I went on. We found my brother and we stopped there. Night fell. We stayed there throughout the night. I fell asleep again. The next day, when it dawned, I saw a lot of dead people around me, they had been killed. Some had been mutilated. After that, my brother wasn't there. I was alone there. I suppose when I fell asleep and the shooting started, they disappeared again. So I went on and found them. There were a lot of people there on a hillside. And what happened then, it was about midday, the sun was out, it was warm and we heard the Serbs from the asphalt road calling out to us to surrender. They were saying, "Surrender, the UNPROFOR is here." I saw a white personnel carrier with a blue helmets. And they said, "Surrender, the UNPROFOR will transport you safely to Tuzla." I had the feeling that if I surrender, I would survive. And I said to my father, let's go and surrender. In fact, I was begging him to. That was the feeling I had. And about 2.00 in the afternoon, we headed downhill towards the asphalt road. Again, we saw UN personnel carriers and blue helmets. As we were coming down, before we reached the road itself, there was a slight climb. There were two Serb soldiers, one on each side standing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, let me interrupt you there for just a minute and let me ask you first of all, do you remember the date it was when you surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was the 13th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to show you a film; you've seen this before in my office. It's a film of your actual surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if I could, Mr. President, have transcripts of the film that I'm going to show disseminated, that would be Prosecutor's Exhibit 103A. Unfortunately, the transcripts are only in English. Then once they are disseminated, I'll ask that the film itself be played. And if the interpreters could please translate as the film is being played. The translation booth has been provided with an English language transcript. Now, if the lights could be dimmed, please, and we could play Prosecutor's Exhibit 103, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover]. I don't know, from some desrt. How long have you been there? We were there two days and two nights. Completely surrounded. What. Where are your rifles? I didn't have a rifle, I am a civilian. A civilian? All right, then have no fear. Were you afraid? Who wouldn't be afraid? Hey, hey, you journalist. How come he already arrived, before they did? Hey, take off that shirt. This one? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, not all of the film and all of the language on the film was translated. I know it's difficult for the interpreters to do it following the film, but the translation that has been provided to the Chamber is a complete translation that has been provided to us by the language service section. Now, if I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 104 placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, I've placed on the ELMO a still image taken from that film we just saw, Prosecutor's Exhibit 103. Is that you in this still image?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's you at the time of your surrender; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Husic, you described in part of your answer that you surrendered because you could hear Bosnian Serbs calling you down to surrender; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Not only because we heard them calling out to us to surrender but also because we saw UNPROFOR there, because we thought that they couldn't simply kill us in the presence of UNPROFOR. We hoped that UNPROFOR would transport us to Tuzla, as the Serbs themselves had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President and Your Honours, I'm going to play another film, and I'd ask that Prosecutor's Exhibit 102A, a transcript from that film, also be distributed to Your Honours before we play the film. Again, if the language booths could try to follow this and translate this film as well. I direct Your Honours' attention just to significant parts of this film. I'll describe it initially. It's Bosnian Serb soldiers calling into the woods for people to surrender, and at the end of film you'll notice an individual wearing a blue UN helmet. So if we could dim the lights, please, and play Prosecutor's Exhibit 102. This is a short film; it only lasts 44 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] How many of them got out already? About three or four thousands. And they all surrendered to you here? Yes. When we give such a figure, people in Belgrade usually say it is exaggerated. Well, it is exaggerated, of course it is. But that is really how many of them. Yes. So much. So much. There they are, look there. See how he disappeared. There, on the left. Come on, boys, get out freely, boys. He was the one who aimed? Five or six passed. Get out, hey. You see them now, do you see them? There is a whole file of them. Two, that's how it goes, one after the other, three. About fifteen passed now. So they are coming down like that all day? Surrender, boys. From this morning. All day they are coming out like that. The last group that passed was 400 of them, they came out down there. Uniforms they leave up there, they dress in civilian clothes and ... You down there, come out. Let's go. Hurry up. Hurry up. Faster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Husic, does that film accurately depict the events as you recall them?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified in your direct examination that you saw white APCs, armoured personnel carriers, belonging to the UN; you saw Bosnian Serbs in blue helmets. Did you also see Bosnian Serb soldiers in UN camouflage flak jackets?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having lived in the enclave and having seen the UN Dutch Battalion soldiers patrolling through the enclave, were you familiar with the UN type of camouflage?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there a lot of Bosnian Serb soldiers wearing UN camouflage flak jackets, as well as the UN blue helmets?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Not that many. I saw between eight and ten of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibits 105, 106, and 107 distributed, first of all, and then placed on the ELMO. These, Mr. President and Your Honours, are, I would say, poor quality still images taken from Prosecutor's Exhibit 103, the film. They are intended to show Your Honours and assist Your Honours, if and when you review the film, with the types of UN flak jackets that are worn by Bosnian Serb soldiers. If you could start, Mr. Usher, by placing Prosecutor's 105 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, these are still images taken from the film of your surrender. Can you tell us what the soldier who is to the left of the man in the blue shirt is wearing?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I can recognise here a UN flak jacket. It is black.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could we have the next exhibit, Prosecutor's 106, placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify what the man, the soldier, on the left-hand side of this image is wearing?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: He's wearing a UN flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point that out with the pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now could we turn to the next image, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit's 107, and place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've seen this from the film. Could you tell the Judges what the soldier on the right side of this image is wearing?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: He's also wearing a UN flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Now, you also had an opportunity to review other film in my office, and I'd like to show you --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like to first of all distribute for the Judges and counsel Prosecutor's Exhibit 101A, which is a transcript in English of the next piece of film footage we're going to show. If we could lower the lights, please, and play Prosecutor's Exhibit 101, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Boro, shall we swap our pistols. Let me see. Do you have a spare one? I do. All right. Want to swap?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise those two soldiers who were in a reclining position, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Judges who those individuals are and what they did to you and to other people who were surrendering.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: These are two Serb soldiers, whom we have just seen on the screen, that were present there. They were asking people for money, German marks, gold, and everything they had on them. They were searching people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the end of this film, you could see a meadow in the film. Is that the location where, after you surrendered, you eventually ended up, on that particular meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to the bags that were being carried by the men who were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Whoever had a bag or a backpack had to leave it before coming out to the meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did they have to leave it?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: They had to leave it by the road, by the asphalt road, on both sides of the road. They were not allowed to take it up to the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if I could have the next series of exhibits taken to the ELMO, they would be Prosecutor's Exhibits 7/2, 7/5, 7/6, and 7/9. Mr. Usher, we'll start with Prosecutor's Exhibit 7/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, have you seen Prosecutor's Exhibit 7/2 in my office?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the dotted yellow line that starts at the top left-hand side of the image, comes down past a house and ends in an oval that is on the left-hand side of the image? Do you see that dotted line?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that dotted line represent your route when you descended from the hills and eventually ended up on the meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me show you the next exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 7/5. Do you recognise what's in this photograph, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can recognise the meadow and the house I passed on the way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you use the pointer, please, and first of all point to the house that you passed on the way down from the mountains.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, Mr. President and Your Honours, the largest house, a little bit off the centre of the picture, on the top side of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the meadow that you ended up on?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating directly below the house on the other side of the road, an area directly off the road. Could we then have Prosecutor's Exhibit 7/6 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, do you recognise what's in this image, Prosecutor's 7/6?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise the rear side of the house, the back part of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to the Judges on which side of the house you passed by when you surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]. On this side of the house, next to these stairs here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, the left-hand side of the image. Lastly, Mr. Usher, if you could place the next exhibit, Prosecutor's 7/9, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a panorama, Mr. Husic. You've had an opportunity to see this in my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could place it a little more to the left, please, so we could show the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that building, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that building?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: It was next to this house [indicates] that I passed on my way, on this side of the house [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could keep moving that image to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the meadow on which you surrendered, Mr. Husic, on this particular panorama?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point it out?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating a green area to the right of the house, below the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you tell the Judges what you saw after you passed the house and after you arrived at the meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I was told to sit down with a group of people, and I went to the left side of the group and I sat down. There were lots of Serb soldiers around us, and to my left was a tank -- I'm sorry, to my right. I could see Serb soldiers coming to the group, asking people for money. They were also taking people away to a nearby cornfield, behind the tank, and they took people away as they pleased. They cursed at them, they cursed at their balija mothers, telling them, "Where is your Alija to help you now? Wait until Ratko Mladic comes here."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Husic, how were those soldiers dressed who were surrounding you in the meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Black camouflage uniform -- green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Would you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: They were dressed in camouflage uniforms but they were different, not all of them were the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the uniforms as best you can recall them, each of the different types of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I can remember that there was a blue police uniform, which was also a camouflage uniform, and a military uniform that was used by the Serbian army. I also remember a multicoloured open uniform, light coloured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many blue police camouflage uniforms did you see while you were at the meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't see a single one, but I could recognise the pattern of the uniform. It was a green camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we have seen in both the films that we've played and the still images, we've seen people in green camouflage uniforms. Is that the type of uniform that you saw, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you estimate approximately how many people were on the meadow when you arrived in the group?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Between 900 and 1.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anybody, any family member that you knew amongst those people on the meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I saw two brothers from the village of Osmac, from the municipality of Srebrenica. And I recognised also Ramo who was calling out to people, the man who was wearing a blue shirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see your father?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see your brother?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were alone on the meadow in so far as your direct family relations?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I'm referring only to the video. But I did see my brother and my father in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you describe for the Judges what you saw the soldiers doing to the people, the Muslim men who were sitting on the meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: The worst. They were cursing at people, they were kicking them, taking them away to the house. There was a relative of mine, Husic Safet, who was taken away in this fashion, and he never came back. I remember a man who was sitting in front of me, he gave 20 German marks to a Serbian soldier wearing glasses. They were taking people away to the cornfield which was behind the tank to the right side. And many of them would come to the group and hit the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you saw some men being taken to a cornfield. Were they Muslim men being taken to the cornfield?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see those -- the -- did Bosnian Serb soldiers take the Muslim men to the cornfields?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see those Bosnian Serb soldiers return from the cornfields without the Muslim men who had been escorted in that direction?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, continue telling the Judges what happened while you were at this particular meadow. What did you do? What were you asked to do?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: While I was sitting there, a soldier who was on the tank, on my right-hand side, he cursed my balija mother and told me to get up. But the man who was sitting next to me stood up because he was confused. He didn't know whom the soldier had in mind. But then he pointed at me. So I stood up and I went to the tank and they gave me two jerrycans, and I was told to go to the asphalt road and to continue along the road, and to my left, that there would be some water. So I took those two jerrycans and I went to the left, down the road, and I filled them with water. I returned to the meadow, and the Serb soldier ordered me to distribute the water around, but not to give too much to each of the men. This is what I did. After I was coming back the second time, I saw a number of Serb soldiers next to the asphalt road. There was a man of my age there, Samir Krdzic and he had been assigned the same task. He had to bring water to the meadow. While I was standing there, a Serb soldier approached me with an automatic rifle and he cursed my mother, and he asked me why I was laughing. And I told him I was not laughing, and he told me not to speak. But then another soldier came to us and he told him not to touch me. And then he left. So while these young men were standing there, a bus arrived from the direction of Potocari carrying women, and it stopped there near the water. The door of the bus opened, and the driver who was driving the bus, he also probably wanted to take some water. He went to the Serb soldiers and he spoke to them. I had been thinking about escaping, I wanted to try something. And then this opportunity presented itself, and I decided to board the bus and then see what happened. So I threw away the jerrycans and I entered the bus. Meanwhile, the driver was talking to the Serb soldiers who were standing nearby. I got on the bus and I hid amongst the women who covered me with some bags. So when the driver came back, he started the engine, he didn't notice me, and he set off. And during our journey, I heard at one point that the bus was being hit with rocks. Local women were probably throwing stones at the bus. So nothing happened, and the bus stopped in Tisca. I got out of the bus. There were some elderly people who could not walk, and I mixed with the women there and I helped them carry an old woman. And this is how I managed to reach the free territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the soldiers, Bosnian Serb soldiers who were in Tisca? What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: They were wearing those same uniforms as those down there, only they looked a little newer to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Describe the uniforms, were they camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Camouflage, yes, camouflage, green and a sort of off white. It's not really white. I don't know how I can describe that colour. Anyway, they were new camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to return to the meadow for one last observation of yours, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 7/4 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified, Mr. Husic, that there was a tank that was on the meadow near the prisoners who were sitting?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 7/4 which is now on the ELMO, and do you see the -- could you point out for the Judges the location of the tank that you remember?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can, here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating for the record the unidentified vehicle on the right side of the image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, lastly, Mr. Husic, I'm going to show you some additional exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibits 108, 109, 110, and 111 disseminated. These, Mr. President, Your Honours, and counsel are still images taken from Prosecutor's Exhibit 103. If we could start, Mr. Usher, with Prosecutor's Exhibit 108.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, this is an image from the film of your surrender. Can you please tell the Judges who these two men are?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: They are the brothers that I mentioned when I was telling you about it, Osman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, these two brothers, to your knowledge, Mr. Husic, did they survive?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did their father survive?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No. He was taken to the cornfield behind the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you another picture of a man who surrendered to the Bosnian Serb army, again taken from your film of your surrender, Prosecutor's Exhibit 109. Do you see the man in the blue shirt in the middle of that image and he's flanked by two Bosnian Serb soldiers? Can you tell us his name?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Ramo is his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Ramo survive?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go to the next image which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 110. Again, an image showing a number of men who were surrendering today Bosnian Serb soldiers. Can you identify any specific individual in this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: On the right, his name is Juso, and did he not survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Point out Juso on the exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, a man who appears to be in a brown-coloured coat or jacket and he's on the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lastly, in this series of exhibits, let me show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 111. First of all, Mr. Husic, do you see yourself in that exhibit?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point out where you are in this image?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating the individual who is the second individual from the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you see the man in the camouflage T-shirt directly in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the judges what happened to that man?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: They ordered him to take off his T-shirt, and they took him to the cornfield and he also did not survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition, Mr. Husic, to these individuals who were shown surrendering to the Bosnian Serb army, were there a number of other individuals you can identify by name who did not survive?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please identify those individuals, who you saw alive on the meadow who not survive?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I know my neighbours, Husic Mehemed, Husic Mehmedalija, Husic Safet, and another man named called Sead Krdzic. They also did not survive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an individual named Sajdin Husic?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is my father who also did not survive. He stayed behind there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question, Mr. Husic, all of these individuals you've seen in the images and who you have named who did not survive, were they Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, thank you, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I've concluded my examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, very much, Mr. Harmon. I think this is a good time for a break before the cross-examination. So we'll have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Husic, have you had some rest during the break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now you will answer questions that will be put to you by Mr. Visnjic, who is counsel for the Defence here. Mr. Visnjic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Visnjic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Husic.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, in your statement, or rather during your direct testimony, you said that while you were going to the woods, and prior to your surrender, that there had been a group of soldiers with you who were armed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That there were 50 of them.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's try to have short breaks between questions and answers. Could you tell me, Mr. Husic, something about those soldiers? Did any of them surrender, of those who had weapons?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you surrendered -- strike that. Could you tell us, please, whether you know where those soldiers with weapons had gone.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you anything about that because I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were on the hill, could you see the Serb soldiers calling out to you from the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far were you from them at that moment? Could you give us an estimate?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them before you decided to surrender or afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise in your questions, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point you saw Serb soldiers there. Was it before or after you reached the decision to surrender?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: We had seen them prior to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean before you reached the decision to surrender.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Husic, how many soldiers, Serb soldiers, approximately, were there at the meadow?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: There were a lot of them. I couldn't tell how many exactly, I couldn't give you the exact number, but they were all over the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were living in Srebrenica before 1995, the last three years preceding 1995.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No. Two years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those two years, did you leave Srebrenica? Did you get out of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those two years, did you ever see Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Excuse me. There was no answer, at least translated, to that question of Mr. Visnjic's, and in order to make the record complete, I think we need an answer to that last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During those two years, for the record, Witness, did you see Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Muslim army that was in Srebrenica, did they have any special uniform?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified in direct about a difference between three kinds of uniforms, that there was a blue police uniform and two other types of uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were all uniforms of the Serb army.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain, then, to me, you didn't leave Srebrenica and you didn't see Serb soldiers during that time, so how do you know that they used to have different kinds of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Well, at the moment I surrendered, I could observe that, and I also saw that later on on TV and I learned that those were Serb uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us an estimate of the number of people who were on the meadow where you were?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Between 900 and 1.000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified during the examination-in-chief about a video film, which has been shown by the Prosecutor, where we could see two Serb soldiers who were identified by you as the soldiers who were searching people for money.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you observe on their uniforms, on their right sleeve, a sign in three colours, with the lettering "Policija" on it?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the location where you surrendered and near the meadow where you were sitting, did you notice a police vehicle of blue and white colours?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your impression, the Serb soldiers who were moving in the area, were they members of one unit or members of various units? Were they just individuals coming in and out? Were those units outside any control? Was there any command?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I could see three different kinds of uniforms, so I don't think that they were members of one and the same unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the TV, the watching of TV after you had crossed over to the free territory. Could you tell us whether you had seen Muslim soldiers on TV, those who had managed to break through to the free territory?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: I didn't see any soldiers; I only saw civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did watch TV.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't watch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached Tisca, you got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you continued on foot.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone approach you, anyone from amongst the Serb civilians or the military? Was there anything special that you could observe at that moment?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Nobody approached me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the name "Ejub Golic" tell you something?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Ejub Golic? Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a commander of a Muslim unit?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: According to what I have heard, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he also take part in the breakthrough?

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that he did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know anything else about that.

utterances.speaker: ENVER HUSIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
